meta.title: End to End 1 of 2 - Intake and Routing

views.label: Authenticate and intake
views.note: Token; tenant + customer from our DB; customerId cross-check; schema then rules, all violations at once; one intake tx (4.1 steps 1-5).

views.label: Relay and route
views.note: One publisher per key bucket; consumers claim the record key first; stage 1 idempotent: ACCEPTED to ROUTED guard + unique (message, route)

views.label: Synchronous variant
views.note: Message and delivery outbox rows deferred; inline stage 1, bulkhead permit, same claim, one call (architecture.md 4.2).

messages.label: get token (client credentials)
messages.note: Every platform-created client has the default audience scope (ADR-007 D3)

messages.label: POST /interfaces/{code}/messages[:bulk] + Bearer + Idempotency-Key
messages.note: Token validated: issuer, JWKS signature, RS256/ES256, aud, exp (ADR-007 D4)

messages.label: ipaas_client_bootstrap(iss, azp): tenant, customer
messages.note: Humans first; then the credential: ACTIVE credentials of ACTIVE tenants only, so a revoke bites at once (ADR-007 D2-D3)

messages.label: 403 body customerId names another customer (recorded)
messages.note: Every customerId / customer_id of the body, per bulk record; none = the credential's customer; nothing stored (ADR-007 D2)

messages.label: bound source: tenant + customer
messages.note: Tenant never from the body or a header: a forged one is ignored and recorded

messages.label: validate each record: contract schema, then rules
messages.note: JSON Schema (networknt, every error) first, then each VALIDATION rule set via platform-config's RuleEvaluationPort (ZEN); all violations in one rejection; rules skipped when the payload is not the contract's object (ADR-003 rule 4)

messages.label: one tx: message + payload + outbox
messages.note: Idempotency key per source credential, 24 h; same key, other body = 422 (ADR-011 D4)

messages.label: relay publishes via the publish port (the Kafka adapter)
messages.note: Fire-and-forget publish + acknowledge; the adapter lives in platform-routing (T-110, ADR-015)

messages.label: record: key = SHA-256(tenant, interface, business key); traceparent header
messages.note: Ids-only value; the row's traceparent is the ONLY header (T-112); the key-bucket advisory lock keeps one publisher per bucket, in order (T-179)

messages.label: claim idempotency_key "outbox:<id>"
messages.note: Consumer-side duplicate guard (T-010): the key is stable per outbox row, so a crash re-publish finds a committed claim - duplicate, acknowledged, no effect (architecture.md section 3, ADR-001)

messages.label: one tx: ACCEPTED to ROUTED + deliveries + outbox
messages.note: Key lock; 0 rows = duplicate; insert on conflict (message, route) do nothing; releases holds

messages.label: DB error: pause partitions, back off
messages.note: A transient database error never poisons a record (ADR-005 D13)

messages.label: inline stage 1, bulkhead permit, claim, one call
messages.note: Message and delivery outbox rows deferred by budget + 5 s (ADR-011 D5)

cards.title: Accepted means stored
items: 202 only after message, payload and outbox commit together
Kafka records carry ids; the payload stays in PostgreSQL

cards.title: Duplicates are harmless
items: Same record twice: the guard's claim detects it; N deliveries, not 2N
Same key, 3 relay instances: published in order

cards.title: Continues in part 2
items: Each delivery outbox row goes to delivery.due
Part 2: claim, bulkhead, send, retry, reconcile
